court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Bharat Pertoleum Corporation Ltd vs Sree Venkateswara Service Station

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Bharat Pertoleum Corporation Ltd (rep. by its Territory Manager) / Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (rep. by its Chief Divisional Manager)
parties.respondent_defendant: Sree Venkateswara Service Station (a regd. Firm rep. by its Managing Partner)

facts_of_case: Bharat Pertoleum Corporation Ltd and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd entered into an agreement with Sree Venkateswara Service Station for dealership. The dealer preferred three suits and original applications for grant of interim injunction. Separate applications were also preferred by the dealer for certain reliefs. The trial court passed an order dated 15.12.2000, which is being appealed.

legal_principles.principle: When a dealership agreement has come to an end by efflux of time, the issue raised in O.S.A.No.67 of 2001 becomes infructuous.
legal_principles.held: In view of the fact that the dealership agreement has now come to an end by efflux of time and the agreement is no more in force, we are not deliberating on the issue raised in O.S.A.No.67 of 2001, which became infructuous.

legal_principles.principle: A show cause notice issued by the Petroleum Corporation calling upon the dealer to give reply as to why his dealership agreement be not terminated is a procedural step that must be followed.
legal_principles.held: Though explanation is called for by issuing the show cause notice, from the petitioner and explanation was offered by the petitioner denying the allegations...

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order was modified to direct the defendants to supply petroleum products to the plaintiff subject to certain conditions.

use_for_drafting: preparing a response to a cheque bounce case
understanding the implications of dishonour of cheque
